A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HBO and contain readable methods, equations, seven tables, four figures, and Appendices A–B. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual and multitask fine-tuning results in Table 1, with original ablations and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Table 1 and the ablations and supplementary experiments in Section 5 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same hierarchical sampling procedure, global and local actors, policy-gradient updates, gradient-norm and perplexity-ratio rewards, and difficulty grouping.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four-domain multitask mixture and eight-language multilingual mixture, evaluated on the same nine tasks. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Prop., Temp., Uni., MultiDDS, MultiUAT, MoS, and MoS+. Comparator membership also matches within the sampling-prior, data-volume, and appendix model-size comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains zero-shot accuracy evaluation, macro-averaging, and sampling 10% of multitask and 20% of multilingual training data. Model configurations, Appendix A training settings, and analysis protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same actor ablations and analyses of difficulty granularity, sampling priors, data volume, easy-example removal, model size, reward functions, and actor update frequency.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or random seeds or reports confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing result-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–7 and plots in Figures 2–4 match. For example, Table 1 retains HBO's Llama-3.1-8B averages of 48.07 for multilingual and 52.28 for multitask evaluation. Appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, including the bilevel formulation and reward definitions, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about autonomous global and local data balancing and performance improvements across three backbones and nine tasks. Contribution scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–5 and Appendix B retain the same interpretations of cyclical sampling, easy-example benefits, model-size effects, and performance/runtime tradeoffs. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: The new acknowledgement identifies the Baskerville Tier 2 HPC service and its operator at the University of Birmingham. This adds computing-environment provenance; Appendix A's hardware and hyperparameters and the code/data access information remain unchanged. It does not establish a setting change or new experimental runs.

R1.justification: Section 2's research positioning and all 72 cited works are retained. Bibliography entries move across pages because of the acknowledgement addition, without changes to related-work coverage.

P1.justification: v2 inserts an Acknowledgement section between the conclusion and references and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose, section order, and appendix structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement shifts the bibliography's starting position and redistributes references across pages 10–16. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–7 retain their content, designs, captions, and page placement.

improvement.justification: v2 improves funding and computing-resource attribution through the new acknowledgement, but the method, evidence, explanations, and training instructions remain unchanged, including Appendices A–B. This limited provenance addition and the resulting bibliography reflow do not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
